rules.title: Only users with the Presenter role can present in Teams meetings
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: Standard attendees should not be able to share content in meetings unless they are given the Presenter role. Restricting who can present limits meeting disruption and inappropriate content.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): set 'Who can present?' to 'Only organizers and co-organizers' (or set AllowParticipantGiveRequestControl to False).
rules.impact: Attendees will need to be promoted to presenter to share content.

rules.title: Dial-in users cannot bypass the meeting lobby
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: Dial-in (PSTN) users are not authenticated through the Teams app. Preventing them from bypassing the lobby stops unknown callers joining meetings directly.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): turn off 'Dial-in users can bypass the lobby' (AllowPSTNUsersToBypassLobby = False).

rules.title: Only invited users are automatically admitted to Teams meetings
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: Users who are not invited should not be let into a meeting automatically; this reduces the risk of data leaks, inappropriate content and malicious participants.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): set 'Who can bypass the lobby' to 'People who were invited' (AutoAdmittedUsers = InvitedUsers).

rules.title: Anonymous users cannot join Teams meetings
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: Anonymous users are not authenticated and may not belong to your organization. Blocking them gives you control over who can access meetings.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): turn off 'Anonymous users can join a meeting' (AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting = False).
rules.impact: Meetings can then only be joined by signed-in users.

rules.title: Anonymous users cannot start Teams meetings
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: If anonymous users can start meetings they can admit others from the lobby without being authenticated, increasing the risk of data leakage.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): turn off 'Anonymous users and dial-in callers can start a meeting' (AllowAnonymousUsersToStartMeeting = False).

rules.title: External participants cannot give or request control in Teams meetings
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: External participants should not be able to take control of shared content; limiting this protects information and reduces inappropriate content sharing.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): turn off 'External participants can give or request control' (AllowExternalParticipantGiveRequestControl = False).

rules.title: Only people in my org can bypass the Teams meeting lobby
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams meeting policy found
rules.description: The Global meeting policy should only let people in your organization (or only invited users / the organizer) bypass the lobby, so external and anonymous participants must wait to be admitted.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Global (Org-wide default): set 'Who can bypass the lobby' to 'People in my org', 'People who were invited' or 'Only organizers and co-organizers'.
rules.impact: External participants and guests wait in the lobby until admitted.

rules.title: Third-party cloud storage services are disabled for file sharing in Teams
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams client configuration found
rules.description: Teams should only allow file sharing through approved storage. Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, ShareFile and Egnyte must all be disabled unless explicitly approved.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Teams settings > Files: turn off all third-party cloud storage options (or set AllowDropbox, AllowBox, AllowGoogleDrive, AllowShareFile, AllowEgnyte to False with Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration).
rules.impact: Users can no longer add these services as storage in Teams.

rules.title: Global app permission policy blocks all or most third-party Teams apps
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams app permission policy found
rules.description: The Global app permission policy must not allow all (or all but a few) third-party apps. It should block them all or allow only an approved list.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Permission policies > Global: under 'Third-party apps' choose 'Allow specific apps and block all others' or 'Block all apps'.
rules.impact: Users can only install third-party apps you have approved.

rules.title: Global app permission policy blocks all or most custom Teams apps
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams app permission policy found
rules.description: The Global app permission policy must not allow all (or all but a few) custom (line-of-business) apps. It should block them all or allow only an approved list.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Permission policies > Global: under 'Custom apps' choose 'Allow specific apps and block all others' or 'Block all apps'.
rules.impact: Users can only install custom apps you have approved.

rules.title: Users can report security concerns in Teams (messaging policy)
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Global Teams messaging policy found
rules.description: Covers the Teams half of CIS 8.6.1: the Global messaging policy must let users report messages as security risks. The Defender report submission policy half (reports go to an internal mailbox) is not evaluated here.
rules.remediation: Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Global: turn on 'Report a security concern' (AllowSecurityEndUserReporting = True), and configure user reported settings in the Defender portal to send reports to an internal mailbox.
